__inputs.name: DS_PROMETHEUS
__inputs.label: Prometheus
__inputs.description: Select the Prometheus data source that scrapes 10.12.1.31:11090.

description: Dedicated HTTP and HTTPS listener panels side by side, with raw request counters, request rates, HTTP 500 responses, mean processing time and network throughput. Matched to the supplied Keycloak 12 / WildFly metrics. Includes JVM, database and worker monitoring.

options.content:
**Target:** `$instance` · **Job:** `$job` · **Server:** `$server` · **HTTP:** `$http_listener` · **HTTPS:** `$https_listener`

HTTP and HTTPS panels are shown side by side. A zero request counter can mean statistics are disabled or no traffic reaches that listener. Mean processing time is empty when no requests are recorded. If a proxy terminates TLS and forwards HTTP, look at the HTTP panels. Metrics scrape UP confirms collection only.

panels.title: Metrics scrape
panels.description: 1 = most recent Prometheus scrape succeeded; 0 = scrape failed. Missing data is shown separately. This does not verify the Keycloak login flow.

panels.title: HTTPS requests - total
panels.description: Raw request counter for the selected HTTPS listener. Counts requests since its statistics were started or last reset; not current users.

panels.title: HTTP requests - total
panels.description: Raw request counter for the selected HTTP listener. Counts requests since its statistics were started or last reset; not current users.

panels.title: JVM uptime
panels.description: Time since the JVM started, in seconds.

panels.title: HTTPS requests - last 5 min
panels.description: Estimated request increase over the last five minutes. Prometheus extrapolation can produce fractional values.

panels.title: HTTP requests - last 5 min
panels.description: Estimated request increase over the last five minutes. Prometheus extrapolation can produce fractional values.

panels.title: HTTPS 500s - last 5 min
panels.description: Estimated increase in listener HTTP 500 responses, not failed logins or all HTTP error statuses.

panels.title: HTTP 500s - last 5 min
panels.description: Estimated increase in listener HTTP 500 responses, not failed logins or all HTTP error statuses.

panels.title: HTTPS and HTTP - side by side
HTTPS requests / second
panels.description: Request rate for only the selected HTTPS listener; excludes HTTP and servlet counters.

panels.title: HTTP requests / second
panels.description: Requests handled by the selected HTTP listener. This includes requests forwarded over HTTP by a TLS-terminating proxy. Excludes HTTPS and servlet counters.

panels.title: HTTPS 500 responses / second
panels.description: Undertow error-count counts HTTP 500 responses; this is not a failed-login count.

panels.title: HTTP 500 responses / second
panels.description: Undertow error-count counts HTTP 500 responses; this is not a failed-login count.

panels.title: HTTPS mean processing time
panels.description: Mean listener processing seconds per request. No requests gives no value. This is not p95/p99 or the complete browser response time.

panels.title: HTTP mean processing time
panels.description: Mean listener processing seconds per request. No requests gives no value. This is not p95/p99 or the complete browser response time.

panels.title: HTTPS network throughput
panels.description: Application traffic on the selected HTTPS listener, not host-interface throughput.

panels.title: HTTP network throughput
panels.description: Application traffic on the selected HTTP listener, not host-interface throughput.

panels.title: HTTPS and HTTP - requests / second
panels.description: Compare the selected HTTPS listener with the selected HTTP listener on the same Undertow server. HTTP growth with HTTPS idle is consistent with a proxy forwarding HTTP; confirm the proxy configuration.

panels.title: HTTPS and HTTP - raw request counters
panels.description: Raw cumulative counters help distinguish zero source values from rate-window issues. Values reset when statistics or the server restart.

panels.title: JVM process CPU
panels.description: JVM process CPU load fraction multiplied by 100. This is not host CPU utilization. Unsupported negative readings are omitted.

panels.title: Heap used / maximum
panels.description: Heap used as a percentage of maximum heap. Thresholds are starting points for review, not alert rules.

panels.title: Live JVM threads
panels.description: Current live JVM thread count.

panels.title: Heap memory
panels.description: Heap memory reported by the JVM.

panels.title: Non-heap memory
panels.description: Non-heap memory includes metaspace and compiled code. Undefined or negative maximum values are omitted.

panels.title: JVM process CPU
panels.description: Reported JVM CPU fraction, converted to percent. This metric is not node CPU utilization.

panels.title: Garbage collections / minute
panels.description: Per-collector counter increase normalized to a minute. Rate graphs need multiple scrapes.

panels.title: Garbage collection time
panels.description: Collection elapsed seconds per wall-clock second. This is not an individual-pause latency histogram.

panels.title: JVM memory pools
panels.description: Memory pool names match the JVM and collector in the supplied snapshot. These names may change after JVM or GC changes.

panels.title: System load average
panels.description: Operating-system load average is not CPU percent. The processor count is shown only as a reference.

panels.title: DB connections in use
panels.description: Connections currently borrowed from KeycloakDS. Zero can mean no usage or disabled pool statistics; it is not a database health check.

panels.title: KeycloakDS connections
panels.description: Pool statistics. Available capacity can include connections that could be created and must not be interpreted as idle physical connections. All-zero values in an active environment warrant checking statistics-enabled.

panels.title: KeycloakDS waits and failures
panels.description: Raw accumulated pool statistics, exported as gauges by this endpoint. Values can reset after restart or statistics reset.

panels.title: I/O worker threads
panels.description: Current thread counts reported by the default I/O worker.

panels.title: Work queues
panels.description: Queued work can help diagnose thread saturation. Zero is a normal value when no work is queued.

title: Keycloak - HTTP and HTTPS Listener Monitoring
